root_cause.text: Including `X86_CR4_FRED` in the `cr4_pinned_mask` required temporarily disabling CR4 pinning before APs are online, which allowed attackers to bypass CR4 pinning protections (such as SMEP and SMAP) by manipulating the CPU online status bit in writable memory.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that temporarily disabling CR4 pinning when an AP is not online allows an attacker to "modify the online bit - a single bit in RW memory - and then disable CR4 pinning and then disable SM*P", and the patch resolves this by removing `X86_CR4_FRED` from `cr4_pinned_mask` in `arch/x86/kernel/cpu/common.c`.
